title: Manual Therapy
shortDesc: Hands-on care to support comfortable movement, alongside an active rehabilitation plan.
metaDescription: Hands-on manual therapy in Islamabad for neck pain, back pain and stiff joints. Joint mobilisation, soft-tissue release and Mulligan techniques at The Muscular Junction.
fullDesc: Manual therapy includes joint mobilisation and soft-tissue techniques selected after assessment. At our River Gardens clinic, hands-on treatment is used alongside exercise and practical advice. Your therapist explains the purpose of each technique, asks for consent and checks your response. Mulligan mobilisation with movement may be considered when appropriate; manipulation is never a requirement for care.
whatWeDo: Full movement and joint assessment before any hands-on treatment
Joint mobilisation, Mulligan mobilisation-with-movement and HVLA where indicated
Soft-tissue release, trigger-point work and dry needling
A short home exercise plan to practise between visits
suitability: Tell your therapist about recent trauma, osteoporosis, neurological symptoms, operations and any medication affecting bleeding. Some techniques may be inappropriate. You can decline hands-on treatment and discuss alternatives.
benefit: The aim is to make meaningful activities more manageable. We agree a functional goal and review whether treatment is helping; improvement and the number of visits vary.

faqs.q: Is manual therapy suitable for everyone?
faqs.a: Tell your therapist about recent trauma, osteoporosis, neurological symptoms, operations and any medication affecting bleeding. Some techniques may be inappropriate. You can decline hands-on treatment and discuss alternatives.

faqs.q: How is the treatment plan decided?
faqs.a: We discuss your goals, assess movement and explain the options. Your response and preferences guide follow-up; there is no fixed package or guaranteed recovery time.

title: Sports Rehabilitation
shortDesc: Progressive rehabilitation for the activities and sport you want to return to.
metaDescription: Sports injury rehabilitation in Islamabad — ACL, hamstring, ankle and shoulder injuries. Criteria-based return-to-sport programmes at The Muscular Junction.
fullDesc: Sports rehabilitation connects recovery with the demands of your sport. We consider your training history, injury and goals before planning a gradual return to loading. Strength, balance and movement tasks help guide progression. Return to sport is a shared decision that may also involve your surgeon, doctor or coach; reduced pain alone does not establish readiness.
whatWeDo: Baseline strength and movement testing, compared side to side
Progressive loading through strength, power and plyometric phases
Sport-specific drills that rebuild change-of-direction confidence
Objective return-to-sport criteria to inform return-to-sport planning
suitability: A suspected fracture, a locked joint, severe swelling or inability to bear weight needs medical assessment. Training restrictions after surgery take priority over generic return-to-sport advice.
benefit: The aim is to make meaningful activities more manageable. We agree a functional goal and review whether treatment is helping; improvement and the number of visits vary.

title: Neurological Rehabilitation
shortDesc: Task-based rehabilitation for movement, balance and daily independence.
metaDescription: Neurological rehabilitation in Islamabad for stroke, Parkinson's, Bell's palsy and nerve injury. Task-specific neuro physiotherapy at The Muscular Junction.
fullDesc: Neurological rehabilitation supports people whose movement has been affected by a nervous-system condition. Goals may include transfers, walking, balance and using an arm in daily activities. Tasks are adapted to ability, fatigue and safety. Family involvement can help carry a plan into the home, with coordination with the wider medical team when needed.
whatWeDo: Task-specific, high-repetition retraining of walking, balance and hand function
Tone, spasticity and contracture management
Falls-risk assessment and balance training
Home programme and hands-on training for family caregivers
suitability: New facial droop, arm weakness or speech changes require emergency care, even if they resolve. Rehabilitation appointments are for ongoing care after medical assessment, not a new stroke.

shortDesc: Play-based movement support, developed with children and their families.
metaDescription: Pediatric physiotherapy in Islamabad for developmental delay, cerebral palsy, torticollis and gait concerns. Child-friendly, play-based sessions at The Muscular Junction.
fullDesc: Pediatric physiotherapy considers a child’s development, movement and participation in family life. Sessions use age-appropriate play and guided practice. Development varies, so assessment and follow-up are more useful than comparison with a single milestone checklist.

Positioning, handling and orthotic advice
Parent coaching so progress continues at home

title: Dry Needling & Cupping
seoTitle: Dry Needling & Cupping Therapy in Islamabad
shortDesc: Understand two optional techniques and how they fit within rehabilitation.
metaDescription: Dry needling and cupping therapy in Islamabad for trigger points, myofascial pain and muscle tightness — delivered by trained physiotherapists at The Muscular Junction.
fullDesc: Dry needling and cupping are different approaches sometimes considered alongside physiotherapy. Needling uses fine needles; dry cupping applies suction to the skin. Neither replaces assessment, exercise or appropriate medical care. This overview explains the distinction and links to the individual treatment pages so you can discuss benefits, uncertainty and risks before deciding.
whatWeDo: Screening for contraindications before any needling
Trigger-point dry needling using single-use sterile needles
Static and moving (myofascial decompression) cupping
Immediate follow-up with movement and loading work
suitability: Needling and cupping are optional and require separate screening and consent. Tell the therapist about blood-thinning medication, pregnancy, skin problems, reduced sensation and previous reactions.

title: Cryotherapy & Cold Therapy
shortDesc: Carefully monitored local cold application as a supporting treatment.
metaDescription: Cryotherapy and cold therapy in Islamabad for acute injury, swelling and post-operative pain — used as part of a wider rehabilitation plan at The Muscular Junction.
fullDesc: Local cold therapy may provide short-term relief after some injuries or procedures. It is a supporting measure rather than a complete rehabilitation plan. Your therapist considers skin condition, sensation, circulation and your stage of recovery before recommending it. This service describes local cold application, not whole-body cryotherapy.
whatWeDo: Assessment of whether cold is appropriate for your stage of healing
Controlled, timed application with skin monitoring
Combined cold and compression for swelling management
Clear guidance on safe use at home
suitability: Reduced circulation, altered sensation and some cold-sensitive conditions can make cold application unsuitable. Do not apply ice directly to skin or continue if the skin becomes painful or unusually pale.

title: Dry Needling
shortDesc: An optional needling technique, considered after screening and informed consent.
metaDescription: Dry Needling at The Muscular Junction, River Gardens, Islamabad. Learn about assessment, suitability and what to expect before booking.
fullDesc: Dry needling uses fine, single-use needles in selected muscle areas. It may be discussed for some muscle-related pain, alongside an active plan. Responses vary and soreness or bruising can occur. Your clinician should explain the evidence, alternatives and risks, including uncommon serious complications such as injury to underlying structures. You do not need to agree to needling to receive physiotherapy.
whatWeDo: Discuss symptoms, medical history and alternatives
Explain risks and obtain consent before needling
Use single-use sterile needles and appropriate hygiene
Check your response and give aftercare guidance
suitability: Tell your clinician about pregnancy, blood-thinning medicines, bleeding disorders, infection, immune problems or needle anxiety. Suitability depends on your history and the proposed treatment area.
benefit: The plan focuses on your daily function and agreed goals. Your response guides whether this approach remains useful; outcomes vary.

faqs.q: What should I discuss before dry needling?
faqs.a: Tell your clinician about pregnancy, blood-thinning medicines, bleeding disorders, infection, immune problems or needle anxiety. Suitability depends on your history and the proposed treatment area.

faqs.q: Can I discuss other treatment options?
faqs.a: Yes. Your therapist should explain alternatives and help you decide on a plan that fits your needs and preferences.

title: Cupping Therapy
shortDesc: A discussion of dry cupping as an optional addition to rehabilitation.
metaDescription: Cupping Therapy at The Muscular Junction, River Gardens, Islamabad. Learn about assessment, suitability and what to expect before booking.
fullDesc: Dry cupping applies suction with cups placed on the skin. Some people seek it for muscle discomfort, but evidence for lasting benefit is limited. Temporary circular marks and soreness can occur. At an assessment, discuss whether it adds anything useful to your rehabilitation and what alternatives are available. This page covers dry cupping; it does not describe wet cupping or bloodletting.
whatWeDo: Discuss the reason for considering cupping
Screen skin health and relevant medical conditions
Explain possible marks, discomfort and uncertain benefit
Review comfort and continue the agreed movement plan
suitability: Skin infection, fragile or damaged skin, reduced sensation and bleeding risk may make cupping unsuitable. Disclose medication and medical conditions, and stop if treatment is uncomfortable.
benefit: The plan focuses on your daily function and agreed goals. Your response guides whether this approach remains useful; outcomes vary.

faqs.q: What should I discuss before cupping therapy?
faqs.a: Skin infection, fragile or damaged skin, reduced sensation and bleeding risk may make cupping unsuitable. Disclose medication and medical conditions, and stop if treatment is uncomfortable.

faqs.q: Can I discuss other treatment options?
faqs.a: Yes. Your therapist should explain alternatives and help you decide on a plan that fits your needs and preferences.

title: Post-operative Rehabilitation

metaDescription: Post-operative Rehabilitation at The Muscular Junction, River Gardens, Islamabad. Learn about assessment, suitability and what to expect before booking.
fullDesc: Post-operative rehabilitation helps you work toward daily function after surgery. The procedure, your health and the surgeon’s instructions determine when and how activities progress. Bring your discharge summary and protocol to your first appointment. We discuss practical goals such as walking, using stairs or returning to work, then review progress without promising a fixed recovery date.
whatWeDo: Review the operation and surgeon’s rehabilitation protocol

Plan safe movement and progressive strengthening
Review milestones and communicate concerns to the surgical team

title: Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy
shortDesc: Assessment and rehabilitation for muscle, joint and tendon problems.
metaDescription: Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy at The Muscular Junction, River Gardens, Islamabad. Learn about assessment, suitability and what to expect before booking.
fullDesc: Musculoskeletal physiotherapy considers how muscles, joints and tendons affect your daily life. The assessment explores symptoms, physical activity, work and the activities you want to regain. Education, appropriately paced exercise and sometimes hands-on treatment can form a plan. A scan is not always needed, and the clinical findings help determine whether further medical assessment is appropriate.
whatWeDo: Explore symptoms and daily activity demands
Assess relevant movement, strength and function
Agree an achievable exercise and activity plan
Review meaningful changes and adapt your programme
suitability: Persistent unexplained symptoms, fever, major trauma or new neurological changes may need medical assessment before rehabilitation. Tell your therapist about other conditions and any recent change in health.
